title:
UN Warns of 16 Hunger Hotspots.
Guinea-Bissau Delays Its Vote.
China's Chip Stocks Soar.
subject: UN Warns of 16 Hunger Hotspots. Guinea-Bissau Delays Its Vote. China's Chip Stocks Soar.
preview_text: Hunger hotspots, a delayed vote, a Chinese chip rally, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: UN agencies warn hunger will worsen in 16 hotspots, Guinea-Bissau's junta delays elections to 2028 and Chinese chip stocks post a record gain.
contents_extra: Why Argentina's new central bank law matters, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: UN Agencies Warn Hunger Will Worsen in 16 Hotspots
paragraphs: UN agencies FAO and WFP say hunger will worsen in 16 hotspots between December 2026 and May 2027, up from 13 in June. El Nino has pushed Southern Africa and Central America's Dry Corridor onto the list. The agencies identified a risk of famine in parts of Sudan and South Sudan.

AP reports the agencies pointed to conflict, soaring fuel costs linked to war in the Middle East and steep aid cuts. Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia and northern Nigeria face the highest concern, AP says. In Sudan, nearly 19.5 million people faced crisis-level hunger or worse in the latest nationwide analysis. Sorghum prices there more than doubled in a year.

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau's Junta Pushes Elections Back to 2028
paragraphs: The BBC reports Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have postponed elections scheduled for next week by two years. A decree moved the presidential and parliamentary vote from 6 December to 26 November 2028. The presidency said there were insufficient "technical, material and financial conditions" to hold the polls as planned.

AP reports the decision came on Thursday, the first anniversary of the coup. The military seized power on Nov. 26, 2025, three days after general elections. It ousted President Umaro Sissoco Embalo before official results were announced. Embalo, living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning last month, AP says.

stories.title: China's Chip Stocks Post a Record Gain After a Policy Pledge
paragraphs: CNBC reports the CSI Semiconductor index climbed 17.6% on Friday, its biggest single-day gain on record, according to Wind Information. The STAR index surged 14%. The rally followed a State Council meeting led by Premier Li Qiang. Officials pledged to strengthen state-backed funds to stabilize markets, according to a Xinhua readout.

Separate data released Friday showed profits at sizeable industrial firms surged 20.1% in October from a year earlier, CNBC reports. That was the fastest pace since May. Gains were concentrated in sectors tied to the AI buildout or higher commodity prices. Consumer-facing manufacturers struggled with weak demand and higher input costs.

deep_dive.title: Why Argentina's New Central Bank Law Matters
paragraphs: AP reports Argentina's Congress voted Thursday to bar the central bank from printing money to pay the government's bills. The Chamber of Deputies approved it 141-0, with 99 abstentions. Under the new charter, the bank's "primary and fundamental mission" will be to preserve the value of the peso, AP says.

History explains the stakes. For generations, governments that overspent turned to the central bank to print pesos, AP says. That fueled repeated currency crises and bouts of hyperinflation. The president's office said the reform ends advances to the Treasury and direct purchases of public debt. It also excludes the economy minister from board meetings.

Bloomberg calls the vote a symbolic victory for Javier Milei, who campaigned on abolishing the monetary authority. But Thursday's vote fell short of the two-thirds majority he needed to restore his original wording. AP reports a president can now replace the bank's leadership with a simple Senate majority. Milei had wanted a two-thirds vote in both houses.

The economy is the next test. AP reports preliminary figures showed Argentina had likely slipped into recession. Annual inflation fell from nearly 300% in early 2024 to 33% last month, AP says. The charter leaves currency controls in the bank's hands. Milei will seek a second four-year term in less than a year.

trivia.question: How many hunger hotspots does the new FAO and WFP report list?
trivia.explanation: The answer is 16. The agencies say the list rose from 13 hotspots in June.
